title: core/types/bal, beacon/engine: unbounded memory allocation in BAL RLP decoding before ValidateSize
body:
### Description

Under EIP-7928 (Amsterdam Block Access Lists), the item count constraint is defined as:

```
itemCount <= block_gas_limit / params.BALItemCost
```

where `params.BALItemCost = 2000`.

Currently, untrusted access lists received via the Engine API (`engine_newPayloadV4`/`V5`) are decoded using `rlp.DecodeBytes` in `attachAccessList` without any item count or size bounds. Because consensus size validation (`block.AccessList().Validate`) only runs later in `ValidateBody`, a payload with an oversized BAL (e.g. 1.5M accounts, ~40+ MB RLP) forces Geth to decode and allocate all `AccountAccess` structs onto the heap before eventually rejecting the block.

This was noted as finding `HACK-03` in the Hackerbane security assessment report:
> *"Reject in attachAccessList (or DecodeRLP with a caller-supplied cap) when encoded length or len(list) exceeds gasLimit / BALItemCost, before allocating per-account objects. Keep ValidateSize as the consensus check."*

### Proposed Solution

1. Add bounded RLP decoding to `BlockAccessList` (`DecodeRLPLimited` / `DecodeBytesLimited`) that stops decoding further accounts once the item budget is exhausted.
2. In `beacon/engine.attachAccessList`, reject payloads early if raw BAL size exceeds `params.MaxBlockSize` (8 MiB), and decode with `bal.DecodeBytesLimited` using `block.GasLimit() / params.BALItemCost`.
